title: Creamy Chili Oil Tomato & Bocconcini Udon with Jammy Eggs
blurb: Born from the leftovers after hosting a party: a creamy, slightly spicy tomato sauce with garlic, wilted spinach, soft bocconcini, lemon and jammy eggs.
ingNote: If using evaporated milk instead of heavy cream, use approximately ½ cup.
steps: # Make the jammy eggs
Bring a pot of water to a boil.
Carefully add eggs and boil for **6½–7 minutes**.
Transfer immediately to an ice bath.
Peel and set aside.
> For firmer yolks, boil for 8–9 minutes.
# Blister the tomatoes
Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Add halved cherry tomatoes.
Season with salt and black pepper.
Cook for **5–7 minutes** until softened and bursting.
Gently press some tomatoes with your spatula to release their juices.
# Build the flavour
Add 1 tbsp butter.
Add minced garlic and sauté for **30–60 seconds**.
Add 1–2 tsp chili oil (start small).
Stir everything together.
> Be careful not to burn the garlic.
# Make the creamy sauce
Lower the heat to medium-low.
Pour in ½ cup cream or evaporated milk.
Add 2–3 tbsp water.
Stir gently until the tomato juices and cream combine.
Simmer for **2–3 minutes** until slightly thickened.
> Taste and adjust salt and pepper.
# Add spinach
Add two handfuls of spinach directly into the sauce.
Stir until wilted, approximately **1–2 minutes**.
# Add udon
Prepare udon according to package instructions.
Drain and add directly to the sauce.
Toss gently until noodles are evenly coated.
Add a splash of water if the sauce is too thick.
> Let everything cook together for 1–2 minutes.
# Add bocconcini and lemon
Turn off the heat.
Add halved bocconcini and gently fold through.
Add 1–2 tsp lemon juice.
Add lemon zest if available.
> Let the residual heat soften the cheese without completely melting it.
# Plate and garnish
Divide udon between two bowls.
Place halved jammy eggs on top.
Drizzle with chili oil.
Finish with black pepper, parmesan and a little olive oil.
> Serve immediately!
tips: **Sauce too thick?** Add water 1 tbsp at a time.
**Sauce too acidic?** Add a little more butter or cream.
**Not spicy enough?** Add more chili oil when plating.
**Cheese not melting?** That's okay! Bocconcini is meant to stay soft and slightly chewy here.
**Lemon:** Always add after turning off the heat to avoid splitting the cream.
notes:
Plate the noodles in a shallow bowl, arrange the bocconcini and cherry tomatoes visibly on top, cut the jammy eggs in half, and finish with a generous chili oil drizzle and cracked black pepper.

**The key is balancing the richness of the cream and cheese with the acidity of the lemon and sweetness of the tomatoes.** Enjoy!

title: Thai Pineapple Fried Rice with Shrimp
blurb: Golden, curry-scented fried rice with juicy shrimp, red pepper, pineapple, raisins and crunchy cashews. Sweet, savoury, nutty and aromatic.
steps: # Prepare your ingredients
Break up cold rice.
Dice pineapple and red pepper.
Pat shrimp dry and season lightly with salt and pepper.
If raisins are particularly dry, soak them in warm water for **5 minutes** and drain.
# Toast cashews
Dry-fry cashews over medium heat until golden. Remove and set aside.
# Cook shrimp
Heat ½ tbsp oil in a wok over medium-high heat.
Cook shrimp for approximately **1–2 minutes per side** until just opaque and cooked through. Remove and set aside.
# Scramble eggs
Add a little oil and scramble eggs until just set. Remove and set aside.
# Sauté aromatics
Add remaining oil. Sauté shallots and garlic until fragrant, about **30–45 seconds**.
# Bloom curry powder
Add curry powder and stir for **15–20 seconds**.
> This releases the aroma and gives the rice its beautiful golden colour.
# Fry the rice
Add rice and toss thoroughly to coat in the curry mixture.
Add soy sauce, oyster sauce, fish sauce, sugar and white pepper.
# Add vegetables and fruit
Add red pepper and edamame. Stir-fry for **1–2 minutes**.
Add pineapple and raisins. Let the pineapple get a little caramelization before tossing everything together.
# Bring everything together
Return shrimp and eggs to the wok. Toss until evenly distributed and heated through.
# Finish
Add green onions and toasted cashews. Taste and adjust seasoning.
tips: Add raisins towards the end so they stay plump rather than burning.
Add shrimp back at the very end to avoid overcooking.
Keep the heat high when frying the rice.
Don't add too much pineapple juice or the rice will become wet.
notes: The final result should be golden, fragrant rice with juicy shrimp, little bursts of sweetness from pineapple and raisins, crunchy cashews and colourful red pepper. Enjoy!

title: Coca-Cola Chicken Wings (可樂雞翼)
blurb: Mom's recipe, and a childhood favourite: wings pan-fried, then braised in Coca-Cola until sticky, glossy and caramelized. Perfect with steamed rice.
ingredients: Coca-Cola, or enough to mostly cover the wings
Dark soy sauce, for deeper colour
steps: # Marinate the chicken wings
Add chicken wings, salt, soy sauce, and cornstarch to a bowl.
Mix until the wings are evenly coated.
Let marinate for **20–30 minutes**.
# Pan-fry the wings
Heat a little oil in a pan over medium heat.
Add the chicken wings in a single layer.
Pan-fry until golden brown on both sides. They don't need to be fully cooked yet.
# Add Coca-Cola
Pour Coca-Cola into the pan until the wings are mostly covered.
Add ginger and garlic if using.
Bring to a boil.
# Simmer
Once boiling, reduce the heat to medium-low.
Let simmer uncovered, turning the wings occasionally so they cook evenly and absorb the sauce.
Continue cooking until the chicken is fully cooked and the Coca-Cola sauce begins to reduce.
# Caramelize
As the liquid reduces, the sauce will become thicker, darker, and glossy.
Turn the wings frequently to coat them in the caramelized sauce.
> Watch carefully towards the end because the sugar in Coca-Cola can burn quickly.
# Serve
Remove from heat once the wings are coated in a sticky glaze.
Serve immediately with steamed rice!
tips: No need to add extra sugar. Coca-Cola already contains plenty.
Keep the pan uncovered while simmering to help the sauce reduce.
If the sauce gets too thick before the wings are cooked, add a splash of water.
Make sure the thickest part of the wings reaches **74°C (165°F)** internally before serving.

title: One-Pan Garlic Sausage Spaghetti
blurb: Garlicky sausage spaghetti tossed in a sweet-savoury ketchup and oyster sauce, all cooked in one pan with no pre-boiling or draining. A total lifesaver back in uni.
ingredients: Vegetables of choice (onion, bell pepper, mushrooms, etc.)
ingNote: One-pan recipe. No need to pre-boil the pasta.
steps: # Sauté ingredients
Heat cooking oil in a large pan.
Add minced garlic, sliced sausage and vegetables.
Stir-fry until fragrant and the garlic is lightly golden.
# Add water
Pour 1 cup of water into the pan and bring to a boil.
# Cook spaghetti
Add uncooked spaghetti.
Cook for **8–10 minutes**, stirring occasionally so the pasta doesn't stick together.
> If the pan becomes too dry before the pasta is cooked, gradually add a little more water.
# Add sauce
Once the spaghetti is cooked, add 3 tbsp ketchup and 1 tbsp oyster sauce.
Stir-fry for another minute until everything is evenly coated.
# Finish
Turn off the heat.
Add a few cracks of black pepper and sprinkle with Parmesan cheese, if desired.
tips: Start with 1 cup of water, but keep extra water nearby.
Stir frequently to prevent sticking.
Adjust the ketchup and oyster sauce to taste.
The final consistency should be saucy but not watery.
notes: One pan, no draining required!

title: Lemon Dill Miso Butter Salmon
blurb: Pan-fried salmon finished under a melting lemon, dill, garlic and miso butter. Bright, savoury and ready in 20 minutes.
steps: **Make the miso butter:** In a bowl, combine softened butter, miso paste, chopped dill, lemon juice, lemon zest, and grated garlic. Mix until smooth.
**Season salmon:** Pat salmon dry with paper towels. Season both sides with salt and black pepper.
**Pan-fry:** Heat oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Once hot, add salmon and pan-fry for **3 minutes on each side**.
> If the butter starts browning or burning, lower the heat before adding it.
**Add miso butter:** Add your desired amount of miso butter on top of the salmon. Cover the pan with a lid and cook for another **3 minutes**, or until salmon is cooked through.
**Garnish:** Top with sesame seeds and green onions.
tips: The miso butter can be stored in the fridge for up to 2 weeks.
You can make extra miso butter and use it on vegetables, mushrooms, or potatoes.
Serve with steamed rice, cucumber salad, or bok choy.
If the butter starts browning or burning, lower the heat before adding it.
notes: Original recipe from Tiffy Cooks (tiffycooks.com), Salmon with Miso Butter.

title: Creamy Mushroom Pesto Pasta
blurb: A rich, creamy pasta with golden sautéed mushrooms, garlic, fresh thyme, basil pesto, heavy cream and Parmesan.
steps: # Prepare the mushroom mixture
Heat 20 g butter and olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat.
Add mushrooms and cook for **5–7 minutes** until golden brown and their moisture has evaporated.
Add shallots (if using) and cook for another **2 minutes**.
Add minced garlic and thyme. Cook for **30–60 seconds** until fragrant.
Season with salt and black pepper.
Remove from heat briefly.
# Cook the pasta
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Add pasta and cook according to package instructions until al dente.
Before draining, reserve at least ½ cup pasta water.
Drain pasta. Do not rinse.
# Make the creamy pesto sauce
In the same frying pan, melt 1 tbsp butter over medium-low heat.
Add your mushroom mixture and warm through.
Add 30 g basil pesto and stir until evenly distributed.
Pour in 100 ml heavy cream.
Stir gently until combined.
Add grated Parmesan.
Simmer gently for **2–3 minutes** until the sauce begins to thicken.
> Avoid boiling the cream vigorously.
# Combine pasta and sauce
Add cooked pasta directly into the pan.
Toss until the pasta is coated in sauce.
Gradually add reserved pasta water, 1–2 tbsp at a time.
Continue tossing until the sauce becomes glossy and clings to the pasta.
Taste and adjust with salt, pepper and additional pesto if desired.
Add a small squeeze of lemon juice to brighten the sauce.
# Garnish and serve
Finish with freshly grated Parmesan, fresh basil leaves, cracked black pepper and a little drizzle of olive oil.
tips: **Mushrooms:** Cook them until golden rather than just softened. This gives the pasta a deeper, more savoury flavour.
**Pesto:** Add before the cream so it distributes evenly throughout the sauce.
**Cream:** Use 35% heavy cream for a richer, thicker sauce.
**Pasta water:** This helps emulsify the sauce and makes it cling to the pasta.
**Thyme:** Keep it! It pairs beautifully with mushrooms and basil pesto.
notes:
**Use up your tart filling:** leftover mushroom mixture from the [[mushroom-gruyere-tarts|Mushroom & Gruyère Tarts]] works perfectly here.

**Favourite combination:** Rigatoni, 35% cream, basil pesto, the Gruyère-tart mushroom filling and lots of Parmesan. The ridges in rigatoni hold onto the creamy sauce really nicely.

title: Taiwanese Popcorn Chicken: Air-Fried
blurb: Craggy, crispy night-market-style popcorn chicken with garlic, five-spice and crispy Thai basil, made in the air fryer.
ingredients: Boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into roughly 1-inch pieces
Coarse tapioca starch (coarse sweet potato starch also works)
Thai basil leaves, picked, washed and thoroughly dried
ingNote: No coarse starch? Regular tapioca or potato starch works best; cornstarch is a last resort. The crust will be smoother and less craggy.
steps: # Marinate
Cut the chicken and combine it with the marinade ingredients.
Cover and refrigerate for at least **30 minutes**.
# Add the egg white
Mix in the egg white until every piece is evenly coated.
# Coat
Put the starch in a shallow dish.
Press each piece firmly into the starch so the coarse granules stick. Rough, uneven coverage is fine.
# First air fry
Spray the basket or tray with oil.
Arrange the chicken in a single layer and spray the tops generously with oil.
Air fry at **375°F (190°C) for 8 minutes**. No need to preheat.
# Flip and crisp
Flip the chicken and spray it again.
Raise the temperature to **400°F (200°C)** and air fry for **6 more minutes**, until golden and crispy.
# Add the basil
Put the completely dry basil leaves in the basket and spray them with oil.
Air fry everything together at **400°F (200°C) for 2 more minutes**.
# Season and serve
Combine the seasoning mix ingredients.
Right after the chicken comes out, sprinkle on as much seasoning as you like (or skip it).
Toss and serve hot.
> The chicken should reach an internal temperature of 165°F (74°C).
tips: You can marinate overnight, but avoid going much past 24 hours, as the texture can change.
Traditional popcorn chicken uses coarse sweet potato starch. Coarse tapioca starch gives a similar craggy crust.
Air fryers vary, so adjust the cooking time slightly if needed.
1 lb of chicken fits in one batch in a 6-quart air fryer. Cook in batches if yours is smaller, so the pieces stay in a single layer.
Serve immediately for the crispiest result.
notes: From The Crystal Cookbook (thecrystalcookbook.com).

title: Bacon Feta Egg Bites
blurb: Little café-style frittatas with crispy bacon, sweet red pepper, spinach and salty feta. Lovely for an easy breakfast through the week.
steps: # Prepare the bacon
Pan-fry bacon until slightly crispy.
Transfer to paper towels to drain excess grease.
Let cool and chop into small pieces.
# Prepare the vegetables
Dice bell pepper into approximately 0.5 cm pieces.
Using a little leftover bacon fat, sauté bell pepper for **2–3 minutes** until slightly softened.
Add spinach and cook until wilted.
Allow excess moisture to evaporate.
# Prepare the egg mixture
In a mixing bowl, whisk together eggs and milk.
Add garlic powder, paprika and black pepper.
Mix until well combined.
# Assemble the egg bites
Grease your 6-cup large muffin tin generously, then layer each cup in this order:
**Bell pepper:** Distribute evenly across the bottom.
**Spinach:** Add the cooked spinach.
**Bacon:** Add chopped cooked bacon.
**Egg mixture:** Pour slowly into each cup until approximately ¾ full.
**Feta:** Crumble feta over the top and gently press some pieces into the egg mixture.
# Bake
Preheat oven to **325°F (160°C)**.
Bake for **22–28 minutes**, until the centres are just set.
A toothpick inserted into the centre should come out without liquid egg.
Let rest for **5 minutes** before removing from the muffin tin.
tips: **Refrigerator:** 3–4 days in an airtight container.
**Freezer:** Up to 2 months.
**Reheat:** Microwave for 30–45 seconds from refrigerated.
notes: **Finishing tip:** Reserve a little bacon, red bell pepper and feta for the tops. The red, green and white colours will make your egg bites look like little café-style frittatas!

title: Korean Soy-Marinated Eggs (Mayak Eggs)
blurb: Jammy eggs soaked in a sweet-salty soy marinade with garlic, chili, scallion and sesame. Perfect over a bowl of steamed rice.
steps: **Boil eggs:** Bring a pot of water to a boil. Gently add eggs and boil for **7 minutes**.
**Ice bath:** Immediately transfer eggs into an ice bath. Let cool completely.
**Peel eggs:** Carefully remove the eggshells.
**Prepare marinade:** In a bowl, combine sugar, soy sauce, water, sesame oil, chili pepper, garlic, scallion, and sesame seeds. Mix until sugar dissolves.
**Marinate:** Place peeled eggs into an airtight container and pour marinade over them, ensuring they are submerged.
**Refrigerate:** Cover and refrigerate for at least **6 hours**, preferably overnight.
**Serve:** Enjoy with steamed rice! Drizzle extra marinade over the rice for flavour.
tips: **Storage:** Keep refrigerated and consume within 3–4 days.
notes: Original recipe: “Korean Soy Marinated Eggs (Mayak Eggs)” by cafemaddy.

title: Mushroom & Gruyère Tarts
blurb: Buttery, flaky puff pastry cups filled with caramelized garlic mushrooms, nutty Gruyère and fresh thyme, finished with Parmesan. Perfect as individual savoury appetizers.
ingredients: Butter or cooking spray, for greasing the muffin tin
ingNote: You'll need a regular 12-cup muffin tin.
steps: # Prepare the mushroom filling
Heat butter and olive oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat.
Add diced mushrooms and cook for **5–7 minutes**, stirring occasionally, until golden brown and their moisture has evaporated.
Add shallots (if using) and cook for another **2 minutes**.
Add minced garlic and thyme. Cook for **30–60 seconds** until fragrant.
Season with salt and black pepper.
Remove from heat and let the mushroom mixture cool completely.
> Make sure the mushrooms are relatively dry before assembling. Excess moisture can make the pastry bottoms soggy.
# Prepare the puff pastry
Preheat oven to **400°F (200°C)**.
Lightly grease the cavities of your muffin tin.
Lightly flour your work surface.
Roll out each puff pastry sheet slightly to even out the thickness.
Cut each sheet into 6 squares, approximately 10–11 cm each.
Gently press each pastry square into a muffin cavity.
Allow the corners to stick up slightly above the edges of the tin.
Prick the bottom lightly with a fork.
# Assemble the tartlets
For each tartlet:
- Add approximately 10 grams of grated Gruyère to the bottom.
- Add 1–2 tablespoons of the cooled mushroom filling.
- Sprinkle a little Parmesan over the mushrooms.
- Brush the exposed pastry edges lightly with beaten egg.
> Don't overfill the cups. Leave a little space for the cheese to melt and bubble.
# Bake
Place the muffin tin on the middle rack of your preheated oven.
Bake at **400°F (200°C) for 20–25 minutes**, until the pastry is puffed and golden brown, and the cheese is melted and bubbling.
Remove from the oven and allow to rest in the muffin tin for **5–10 minutes**.
Carefully loosen the edges with a small knife and transfer to a cooling rack.
# Garnish and serve
Finish each tartlet with a few fresh thyme leaves, a tiny Parmesan shaving and freshly cracked black pepper.
> For something a little more special, add a very small drizzle of honey. It complements the earthy mushrooms and nutty Gruyère beautifully.
tips: **Keep pastry cold:** Work with one sheet at a time. If the pastry becomes too soft, refrigerate it for 10 minutes.
**Cook mushrooms thoroughly:** Don't rush this step. Removing moisture is key to crispy pastry.
**Cool the filling:** Hot mushrooms can soften the raw pastry before baking.
**Don't overfill:** You want visible mushrooms and cheese without overflowing.
**Check the bottoms:** If they're still pale, give them another 2–3 minutes in the oven.
notes:
**Make-ahead tip:** You can prepare the mushroom filling a day ahead and refrigerate it. Assemble the tartlets just before baking for the flakiest pastry.

The ideal result: rustic golden pastry edges, a generous mushroom filling, melted Gruyère underneath and little thyme leaves on top.

**Leftover mushroom mix?** Save any extra filling for the [[creamy-mushroom-pesto-pasta|Creamy Mushroom Pesto Pasta]]. About 100–150 g is enough for two servings.

title: Pesto Puff Pastry Squares
blurb: Flaky puff pastry squares spread with basil pesto and topped with cherry tomatoes and Parmesan. Savoury, golden and so pretty on a grazing table.
steps: **Thaw puff pastry:** Let the pastry thaw in the fridge until pliable but still cold. Don't let it become warm or sticky.
**Prepare pastry:** Roll it out gently on a lightly floured surface. Cut into equal squares, one per piece.
**Score the edges:** Lightly score a smaller square inside each piece, leaving approximately a 1 cm border. Don't cut all the way through.
**Add pesto:** Spread approximately 5 grams of pesto in the centre of each square, staying within the scored border.
**Add toppings:** Cut cherry tomatoes in half and place 1–2 halves on each square. Sprinkle with Parmesan and black pepper.
**Egg wash:** Beat egg with water and brush the pastry borders.
**Bake:** Bake at **400°F (200°C) for 18–22 minutes**, until puffed and golden brown.
**Garnish:** Allow to cool slightly. Finish with fresh basil and a little extra Parmesan.
tips: Add a tiny basil leaf on each square after baking.
Use halved cherry tomatoes with the cut side facing up.
Arrange on a vintage silver tray or wooden serving board.
notes:
**Keep them small:** around 5–6 cm squares.

Made with **Vincenzo's basil pesto**.

title: Lemon Vanilla Madeleines
blurb: Little bear-shaped madeleines with vanilla, a whisper of lemon zest and golden, springy tops. Too cute to resist, and always a crowd favourite.
ingNote: Makes approximately 10–12 small madeleines, depending on your bear-shaped mold.
steps: # Whip the eggs
Add eggs, sugar, vanilla extract, and lemon zest to a mixing bowl.
Beat with an electric mixer for **6–7 minutes**, until pale, thick, and fluffy.
# Add dry ingredients
Sift together flour, baking powder, and salt.
Gently fold the dry ingredients into the egg mixture using a spatula.
Fold just until incorporated. Avoid deflating the batter.
# Incorporate butter
Slowly drizzle in the melted butter.
Gently fold until fully incorporated and the batter is smooth.
# Chill the batter
Cover the bowl and refrigerate for **45 minutes**.
# Prepare the mold
Lightly spray your bear-shaped madeleine pan with cooking oil.
Fill each cavity approximately **70–75% full**.
Don't overfill, as the batter will rise.
# Bake
Preheat oven to **350°F (175°C)**.
Bake for approximately **12–15 minutes**, depending on the size of your molds.
Look for lightly golden edges and tops that spring back when gently touched.
# Remove and cool
Let madeleines rest in the pan for **2–3 minutes**.
Gently release them and transfer to a wire cooling rack.
Allow to cool completely.
tips: Lightly respray the pan between batches.
Wipe away any crumbs or residue before refilling.
If making multiple batches, keep the remaining batter refrigerated.
For the prettiest bear shapes, avoid overfilling the ears and paws.
notes: These are lovely with a light dusting of icing sugar once cooled, or dipped halfway in white chocolate for a cute bear-shaped finish! 🤎

title: Matcha Mochi Brownies
blurb: Chewy, bouncy brownies made with glutinous rice flour and plenty of matcha, dusted green on top.
ingNote: Keep the eggs as 2 large eggs — more practical than weighing them.
steps: # Preheat
Preheat oven to **175°C / 350°F**.
# Warm the matcha mixture
Over medium heat, whisk together **300 g water, 50 g butter, 27 g oil, and 10–12 g matcha** until smooth and the butter has melted.
Remove from heat.
# Mix the dry ingredients
In a large bowl, mix **360 g glutinous rice flour**, **250 g sugar**, **3 g salt** and **2–2.5 g baking soda**.
# Combine
Pour the warm matcha mixture into the dry ingredients and stir.
Add **2 eggs + 5 g vanilla** and mix until completely smooth.
# Pan and bake
Pour into a greased or parchment-lined **{pan} pan**. Tap the pan on the counter a few times to remove air bubbles.
Bake for **45–50 minutes**, until a toothpick comes out clean.
# Cool and dust
Cool for **10 minutes** before cutting.
Sift extra matcha over the top if you want a stronger matcha flavour.
notes:
Use **12 g matcha** if you want these to taste noticeably matcha-forward. 10 g will be a little more subtle.

Original recipe: “Easiest Matcha Mochi Brownie Recipe” by Kirby, Eating with Kirby (eatingwithkirby.com).

title: Chocolate Brownies
blurb: Rich, fudgy chocolate brownies made with melted chocolate chips, butter and a little cocoa.
steps: # Preheat oven
Preheat oven to **160°C (320°F)**.
Line your **{pan}** baking pan with parchment paper.
# Melt chocolate and butter
Combine chocolate chips and butter in a heatproof bowl. Melt using either method:

- **Double boiler:** Place the heatproof bowl over a pot of gently boiling water, making sure the bottom of the bowl does not touch the water. Stir until the chocolate and butter are completely melted and smooth.
- **Microwave:** Heat in 20-second intervals, stirring between each interval until smooth.
> Be careful not to let any water or steam get into the chocolate mixture.
# Prepare egg mixture
In another bowl, whisk together eggs, sugar, salt and vanilla extract until combined.
# Combine
Pour the egg mixture into the melted chocolate mixture and mix well.
# Add dry ingredients
Sift together the flour and cocoa powder.
Add to the chocolate mixture and stir until just combined.
# Transfer batter
Pour the batter into the prepared baking pan and spread evenly.
# Bake
Bake at **160°C (320°F) for 30–35 minutes**.
# Cool
Let the brownies cool completely before cutting into squares so they can set properly.
notes: Original recipe: “Chewy Moist Brownies” by 꿀키 Honeykki (YouTube).

title: ChaTraMue Thai Milk Tea
blurb: Strong-steeped ChaTraMue tea sweetened with condensed milk, poured over ice and finished with a float of evaporated milk.
steps: # Brew the tea
Bring **180 g water** to a boil.
Add **10 g tea leaves** and steep for **5 minutes**.
Strain the tea, pressing gently to extract the flavour.
# Sweeten
Stir **40 g condensed milk** and **10 g sugar** into the hot tea until dissolved.
# Pour over ice
Fill a glass with **150–200 g ice** and pour the tea over it.
Pour **15 g evaporated milk** on top and stir before drinking.

title: Shortbread Cookies: Original, Matcha & Chocolate
blurb: Buttery cut-out shortbread that's perfect for cookie cutters, in original, matcha or chocolate. Make each flavour as its own batch for equal amounts.

variants.name: original
ingredients: Unsalted butter, softened to room temperature
Vanilla bean paste or vanilla extract
steps: ## Make, roll & bake
**Cream the butter and sugar.** Mix the softened butter and sifted powdered sugar until smooth and creamy. A hand mixer on low to medium speed is perfect.
**Add the wet ingredients.** Mix in the egg yolk and vanilla until well combined.
**Add the flour.** Sift in the flour and mix until a soft dough forms. Switch to a spatula or wooden spoon here and finish gently with your hands. Avoid overmixing.
**Chill the dough.** Wrap tightly in plastic wrap and freeze for **30 minutes**.
**Roll and cut.** Roll the dough on a lightly floured surface to approximately **3–5 mm** thick. Cut into shapes using your favourite cookie cutters.
**Arrange the cookies.** Transfer them to a baking tray lined with parchment paper or a silicone baking mat.
**Chill again.** Preheat the oven to **150°C (300°F)**. While it preheats, place the cut-out cookies in the fridge.
**Bake.** Bake for **15–20 minutes**, until the edges are just lightly golden. Check early if your cookies are small or thin.
> Don't wait for the whole cookie to turn golden. They should stay fairly pale, with only a hint of colour at the edges.
**Cool.** Let the cookies rest on the tray for **5 minutes**, then transfer them to a cooling rack.
## Making the dough ahead (optional)
# Option A: refrigerate overnight
> Best if you're baking tomorrow. You don't need the 30-minute freeze if you're refrigerating overnight.
Prepare the dough completely.
Shape it into a flat disc and wrap it tightly in plastic wrap, or put it in an airtight container.
Refrigerate for up to **2 days** for best quality.
Tomorrow, let it sit at room temperature for about **5–15 minutes**, just until it is workable.
Roll, cut, and bake as usual. Chill the cut-out cookies in the fridge before baking.
# Option B: freeze overnight
> Best if you want to make the dough well in advance.
Prepare the dough and shape it into a flat disc.
Wrap it tightly in plastic wrap, then place it in a freezer-safe bag or container.
Freeze overnight.
Transfer it to the fridge to thaw for several hours or overnight until rollable.
Roll, cut, chill the shapes in the fridge, and bake.
# Option C: cut the shapes tonight
Cut out all the shapes tonight and arrange them on a parchment-lined tray.
Cover well and refrigerate overnight, then bake straight from the fridge tomorrow.
> Or freeze the cut shapes on a tray until firm, store them in a sealed container with parchment between layers, and bake from frozen, adding a few extra minutes if needed.
tips: **Butter:** soft enough to press a finger into, but not melted.
**Hand mixer:** start at low speed with the powdered sugar to avoid a cloud of sugar. No need to whip in lots of air. This is shortbread, not a fluffy cake.
If the dough is crumbly, knead it gently with your hands until it comes together. If it's genuinely too dry, add a tiny amount of softened butter rather than water.
For all three flavours, aim for a dough that holds together without sticking excessively to your hands.

**Three flavours:** make three separate batches if you want equal amounts of each. Mix the butter and sugar separately for each batch, or only divide plain dough after all its ingredients are incorporated.

variants.name: matcha
ingredients: Unsalted butter, softened to room temperature
Vanilla bean paste or vanilla extract
variants.ingNote: Replace 3 g of the flour with matcha. Sift the matcha together with the flour. Use 4 g matcha (and 96 g flour) for a stronger, more vibrant flavour.
steps: ## Make, roll & bake
**Cream the butter and sugar.** Mix the softened butter and sifted powdered sugar until smooth and creamy. A hand mixer on low to medium speed is perfect.
**Add the wet ingredients.** Mix in the egg yolk and vanilla until well combined.

**Add the flour and matcha.** Sift the matcha together with the flour into the bowl, then mix until a soft dough forms. Switch to a spatula or wooden spoon and finish gently with your hands. Avoid overmixing.
> Keep the matcha dough covered while you work, since matcha can lose its colour when exposed to light and air.
**Chill the dough.** Wrap tightly in plastic wrap and freeze for **30 minutes**.
**Roll and cut.** Roll the dough on a lightly floured surface to approximately **3–5 mm** thick. Cut into shapes using your favourite cookie cutters.
**Arrange the cookies.** Transfer them to a baking tray lined with parchment paper or a silicone baking mat.
**Chill again.** Preheat the oven to **150°C (300°F)**. While it preheats, place the cut-out cookies in the fridge.
**Bake.** Bake for **15–20 minutes**, until the edges are just lightly golden. Check early if your cookies are small or thin.
> Don't wait for the whole cookie to turn golden. Keep them fairly pale, with only a hint of colour at the edges, to preserve the green matcha colour.
**Cool.** Let the cookies rest on the tray for **5 minutes**, then transfer them to a cooling rack.
## Making the dough ahead (optional)
# Option A: refrigerate overnight
> Best if you're baking tomorrow. You don't need the 30-minute freeze if you're refrigerating overnight.
Prepare the dough completely.
Shape it into a flat disc and wrap it tightly in plastic wrap, or put it in an airtight container.
Refrigerate for up to **2 days** for best quality.
Tomorrow, let it sit at room temperature for about **5–15 minutes**, just until it is workable.
Roll, cut, and bake as usual. Chill the cut-out cookies in the fridge before baking.
# Option B: freeze overnight
> Best if you want to make the dough well in advance.
Prepare the dough and shape it into a flat disc.
Wrap it tightly in plastic wrap, then place it in a freezer-safe bag or container.
Freeze overnight.
Transfer it to the fridge to thaw for several hours or overnight until rollable.
Roll, cut, chill the shapes in the fridge, and bake.
# Option C: cut the shapes tonight
Cut out all the shapes tonight and arrange them on a parchment-lined tray.
Cover well and refrigerate overnight, then bake straight from the fridge tomorrow.
> Or freeze the cut shapes on a tray until firm, store them in a sealed container with parchment between layers, and bake from frozen, adding a few extra minutes if needed.
tips: Use unsweetened matcha powder, not a sweetened drink mix.

Sift the matcha thoroughly with the flour to avoid green clumps.
Keep the matcha dough covered while working, since matcha can lose its colour when exposed to light and air.

For all three flavours, aim for a dough that holds together without sticking excessively to your hands.

**Three flavours:** make three separate batches if you want equal amounts of each. Mix the butter and sugar separately for each batch, or only divide plain dough after all its ingredients are incorporated.

title: Hong-Kong Style Egg Tarts: The Shortcut
blurb: Silky, just-set custard in ready-to-bake tart shells. A quick shortcut that skips making pastry, so warm egg tarts are just a whisk and a bake away.
ingNote: Keep the frozen tart shells frozen until you're ready to fill them.
steps: # Prepare the sugar syrup
Combine 35 g icing sugar with 75 g hot water.
Stir until completely dissolved.
Let cool to room temperature.
# Make the custard
Gently whisk 1 whole egg and 1 egg yolk.
Add 30 g evaporated milk, ¼ tsp vanilla extract and a tiny pinch of salt.
Slowly pour in the cooled sugar syrup.
Mix gently until combined.
Strain through a fine-mesh sieve twice for a silky custard.
# Fill the tart shells
Keep your frozen tart shells frozen.
Arrange all 6 shells on a baking tray.
Pour custard into each shell, filling approximately **75–80% full**.
Avoid overfilling as the custard can puff slightly during baking.
# Bake
Bake at **375°F (190°C)** for **22 minutes** (20–25 min).
Start checking at **18 minutes**.
> Look for set custard edges, a centre with a slight jiggle, and no liquid custard when gently shaken.
# Cool
Let the tarts cool for **10–15 minutes** before eating.
> The custard will continue setting as it cools.
tips: Strain twice for a smooth, silky custard.
Avoid whisking vigorously to prevent air bubbles.
Don't overbake, or the custard may crack.
Keep the tart shells frozen until ready to fill.
notes: This is the saved version with **35 g icing sugar and 75 g hot water**. Enjoy! ❤️

title: Purple Sweet Potato Mochi Balls
blurb: Soft, chewy purple sweet potato and glutinous rice balls, air-fried until lightly golden outside.
ingredients: Purple sweet potato, steamed and mashed
Sugar-free maple syrup (or honey / sweetener of choice)
Milk of choice, as needed (if the dough is too dry)
ingNote: The 250 g sweet potato is an approximate conversion for 1 cup mashed sweet potato.
steps: # Steam the sweet potato
Steam until fork-tender, then mash until completely smooth.
# Make the dough
Add glutinous rice flour and maple syrup.
Mix until a soft, pliable dough forms.
If the dough is too dry or crumbly, gradually add milk.
# Shape
Roll into bite-sized balls and arrange in an air fryer basket lined with parchment paper.
# Air-fry
Air-fry at **180°C** for **10–12 minutes**, or until lightly golden on the outside while remaining soft and chewy inside.
# Enjoy warm!
tips: Add milk gradually. The dough should be soft but not sticky.
If you prefer a chewier, mochi-like texture, avoid adding too much extra flour.
Cooking time may vary depending on the size of your mochi balls and air fryer.

title: Classic Blueberry Muffins
blurb: A family favourite: soft, fluffy muffins packed with fresh blueberries and finished with a lightly crunchy sugar top.
steps: # Preheat oven
Preheat oven to **375°F (190°C)**.
Line a 12-cup muffin tin with paper liners.
Lightly grease the liners with nonstick cooking spray.
# Cream butter and sugar
In a large mixing bowl, use a hand mixer to cream together softened butter and sugar for approximately **2 minutes**, until light and fluffy.
# Add eggs and flavourings
Beat in the eggs until combined.
Add baking powder, salt, and vanilla extract. Mix briefly.
# Add flour and milk
Add half of the flour and mix with the hand mixer until just combined.
Add half of the milk and mix.
Scrape down the bottom and sides of the bowl.
Add the remaining flour and milk, mixing between additions until just combined. Avoid overmixing.
# Fold in blueberries
Add the fresh blueberries and gently fold them into the batter using a rubber spatula.
# Fill muffin tin
Divide the batter evenly among the muffin cups.
Sprinkle approximately 1 teaspoon of granulated sugar over each muffin.
# Bake
Bake at **375°F (190°C)** for approximately **30 minutes**, or until a toothpick inserted into the centre comes out clean.
# Cool
Let the muffins cool in the pan for **5 minutes**.
Remove and transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.
tips: Gently fold in blueberries to avoid crushing them and turning the batter purple.
Don't overmix once the flour is added, as this can make the muffins dense.
The sugar topping creates a slightly crunchy, sparkling muffin top.

title: Japanese Milk Buns
blurb: Soft, fluffy milk buns made without eggs, with a tender crumb and a light dusting of cornstarch on top. First baked for a grade 12 science project, and a favourite ever since.
ingredients: Salt (add after the dough comes together)
steps: **Preheat oven.** Preheat oven to **180°C (350°F)**.
**Prepare yeast mixture.** Combine warm milk and instant yeast. Mix well and set aside.
**Combine ingredients.** In a large mixing bowl, add flour and sugar. Pour in the milk and yeast mixture. Mix until the dough comes together.
**Add salt.** Once the dough has come together, add salt and mix it in.
**Knead the dough.** Knead by hand for approximately **5 minutes**.
> If the dough feels too tough or difficult to work with, cover with plastic wrap and let it rest for 20 minutes before continuing.

**Incorporate butter.** Flatten the dough and spread the softened, spreadable butter over the surface. Fold the dough over itself repeatedly to incorporate the butter. Continue folding and kneading until all the butter is fully incorporated.
**First proof.** Transfer the dough into a greased bowl. Lightly grease the top of the dough as well. Cover well and let rise for approximately **2 hours**, or until doubled in size.

**Shape the buns.** Transfer the dough onto a very lightly floured surface. Divide into equal portions, one per bun (12 for a single batch). Weigh each portion for consistent-sized buns, if desired. Shape each portion into a smooth bread roll.
**Second proof.** Place the rolls onto a lined baking tray, leaving space between each bun to allow for expansion. Cover and let rise for an additional **30 minutes**.
**Dust with cornstarch.** Lightly dust the tops of the buns with cornstarch.
**Bake.** Bake at **180°C (350°F) for 18–20 minutes**, until cooked through and lightly golden.
**Cool.** Remove from the oven and allow the buns to cool for **10 minutes** before serving.
tips: If the dough feels tough, let it rest for 20 minutes to relax the gluten before kneading.
Butter should be softened and spreadable, not melted.
Make sure the dough doubles in size during the first proof.
Leave enough space between buns for expansion during the second proof.
notes: Original recipe: “Fluffy Japanese Milk Bread Recipe (The SOFTEST Dinner Rolls)” by Emma's Goodies.

title: Iced Biscoff Latte
blurb: Biscoff melted into hot espresso, poured over cold milk and ice, and topped with a soft Biscoff cream. A cozy cookie-butter treat in a glass.
steps: # Make the Biscoff espresso
Brew your double espresso directly into a small cup.
Add 30 g Biscoff spread while the espresso is hot.
Whisk thoroughly until the Biscoff is completely melted and incorporated. You should have a smooth, thick coffee mixture.
# Prepare the cream
Whisk 40 g whipping cream, 10 g milk and 10 g Biscoff spread until thick but still pourable.
# Assemble
Add ice to your serving glass and pour in 150 g milk.
Slowly pour the Biscoff espresso mixture over the milk.
Top with Biscoff cream.
Garnish with crushed Biscoff biscuits.
notes: Don't add extra sweetener. With the Biscoff in the espresso and more in the cream, it'll already be quite sweet and have a strong cookie butter flavour. ☕

title: Matcha Lattes
blurb: One iced matcha latte, five ways. Pick a flavour, then add its syrup from the Syrups tab.

variants.name: Classic
variants.ingNote: Make the simple syrup from the Syrups tab.
steps: Sift matcha powder into a bowl.
Add 50 g hot water and whisk until smooth and frothy.
Add 15–20 g simple syrup to a glass.
Add ice and pour in 150–175 g milk.
Slowly pour the prepared matcha over the milk.
tips: Whisk the matcha with water at 75–80°C, not boiling, until smooth and frothy.
Pour the matcha slowly over the milk for pretty layers.

steps: Add 25–30 g pear vanilla syrup to the bottom of your glass.
Add ice.
Pour in your milk.
Slowly pour your prepared matcha over the milk.
tips: Use 30 g syrup if you want the pear to be a prominent flavour.
Use 25 g if you want the matcha to remain the star.

tips: Whisk the matcha with water at 75–80°C, not boiling, until smooth and frothy.

Honey stiffens when it's cold, so loosen it with a little warm water before adding ice.

title: Rosemary-Infused Honey Yuzu Tea
blurb: Bright yuzu sweetened with rosemary-infused honey: citrus-forward, with a subtle herbal sweetness. Serve it iced and still, iced and sparkling, or hot.

variants.name: iced, still
variants.ingNote: A more traditional tea-like drink: gentle and mellow.
steps: Stir the rosemary-infused honey with a little warm water first to dissolve.
Add the yuzu concentrate and stir.
Fill the glass with ice.
Pour in 150 g cold water and stir.
Taste and adjust sweetness or yuzu intensity.

variants.name: iced, sparkling
variants.ingNote: Bright, bubbly and refreshing. My pick!
steps: Stir the rosemary-infused honey with a little warm water first to dissolve.
Add the yuzu concentrate and stir.
Fill a tall glass with ice.
Top with 150 g sparkling water and stir gently to keep the bubbles.
Garnish with a rosemary sprig and a thin lemon wheel.
tips: The rosemary honey and yuzu pair beautifully with carbonation, and it makes the drink feel lighter and more refreshing.
Serve in a tall glass with ice. It looks especially pretty with the golden yuzu colour.

variants.name: hot
steps: Add yuzu concentrate and rosemary-infused honey to a glass.
Pour in 200 g hot water.
Stir until dissolved.
Taste and adjust sweetness or yuzu intensity.
tips: Recommended ratio: 25 g yuzu + 15 g rosemary honey + 200 g hot water keeps it citrus-forward with a subtle herbal sweetness.

notes: Make the rosemary-infused honey from the Syrups tab first. Sparkling is the one to put on the home café menu.

title: Simple Syrup
blurb: Plain 1:1 sugar syrup for any drink that needs a little sweetness.
ingNote: Use 15–20 g per latte in the classic matcha latte.
steps: Add the water and sugar to a pot.
Heat over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally until the sugar completely dissolves.
Once the sugar has dissolved, turn off the heat. There's no need to boil it.
Allow the syrup to cool completely.
Transfer to a clean, airtight glass bottle and refrigerate.
notes: **Storage:** Refrigerate in a clean, airtight bottle and use within 1–2 weeks for best quality.

title: Earl Grey Syrup
blurb: A bergamot-scented Earl Grey tea syrup.
ingNote: Use 15–20 g per latte in the Earl Grey matcha latte.
steps: Add the water, sugar, and 3 tea bags to a pot.
Heat over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally until the sugar completely dissolves.
Once the mixture reaches a gentle simmer, turn off the heat. Avoid a prolonged rolling boil.
Let the tea bags steep in the hot syrup for **3–5 minutes**.
Remove the tea bags and gently squeeze out excess liquid.
Allow the syrup to cool completely.
Transfer to a clean, airtight glass bottle and refrigerate.
tips: Avoid a prolonged rolling boil. Turn the heat off as soon as the syrup reaches a gentle simmer.
Gently squeeze the tea bags when you take them out so you don't waste any syrup.
notes: **Storage:** Refrigerate in a clean, airtight bottle and use within 1–2 weeks for best quality.

title: Pear Vanilla Syrup
blurb: A fragrant, lightly floral pear syrup that's sweet without overpowering matcha. Bartlett pears bring a naturally honey-like sweetness.
ingNote: Vanilla bean paste can be swapped for 3–4 g vanilla extract, but the paste gives you those pretty vanilla specks. Use 25–30 g per latte in the pear vanilla matcha latte.
steps: Peel, core, and dice your Bartlett pear into small cubes.
Add pear, sugar, and water to a small saucepan.
Bring to a gentle simmer over medium-low heat.
Simmer uncovered for **15–20 minutes**, stirring occasionally. Lightly mash the pears as they soften.
Remove from heat and stir in vanilla bean paste, lemon juice, and salt.
Let steep for another **10–15 minutes**.
Strain through a fine-mesh sieve. Gently press the fruit to extract the juice, but avoid aggressively squeezing it if you want a clearer syrup.
Cool completely and refrigerate in a sterilized jar.
tips: Add a tiny amount of vanilla bean paste for pretty vanilla specks.
**Don't boil the syrup aggressively.** A gentle simmer preserves the fresh Bartlett pear aroma rather than turning it into a cooked pear or jam-like flavour.
Strain gently. Pressing the fruit too hard makes a cloudier syrup.
notes: Cool completely and refrigerate in a sterilized jar.

title: Rosemary-Infused Honey
blurb: Golden honey gently warmed with fresh rosemary for a soft, herbal sweetness.
ingNote: Use 15 g per drink in the rosemary-infused honey yuzu tea.
steps: Add honey, water and rosemary to a small pot.
Warm over low heat for **5–8 minutes**. Do not boil.
Remove from heat and let steep for another **10–15 minutes**.
Remove rosemary sprigs and let cool.
Transfer to a clean jar.
tips: Keep the heat low. Boiling the honey dulls its flavour and can make it bitter.
